Below is a **complete, minimal HTML file** that shows a MapLibre GL JS map using only a CDN – no npm, no bundler, no build step. ```html MapLibre GL JS – CDN example
``` ### Why it works (v6-specific notes) | What changed in v6? | How the example handles it | |---------------------|----------------------------| | **ESM-only build** – the old `dist/maplibre-gl.js` (UMD) was removed. | The script tag uses `type="module"` and imports `dist/maplibre-gl.mjs`. | | **No default export** – `import maplibregl from 'maplibre-gl'` no longer works. | We import the **namespace** (`* as maplibregl`) or you can do `import { Map, NavigationControl } from '…'`. | | **No `setWorkerUrl()` needed** for CDN usage. | The worker URL is auto-derived from `import.meta.url` when the module is loaded from a CDN, so nothing extra is required. | | **Pin the version** – an un-pinned `@latest` will silently break when a new major version ships. | The URL explicitly uses `@6.15.0` (replace with the exact version you want). | ### Quick checklist before you open the file 1. **Serve it over HTTP** – most browsers block ES-module imports from `file://`. - Run a tiny static server (`python -m http.server`, `npx serve`, etc.) or drop the file into any web server you already have. 2. **Internet connection** – the style URL (`https://demotiles.maplibre.org/style.json`) and the CDN assets are fetched from the web. 3. **Optional custom style** – replace the `style` URL with your own style JSON or a local file (if you host it yourself). That’s it! Open the page in a browser and you’ll see a world map rendered by MapLibre GL JS, all without any build tools or npm. Enjoy!
